'''James Gegan Miller''' is an American [[physicist]], [[engineer]], and [[inventor]] whose primary interests center around biomedical physics. He is currently a professor of physics, Medicine, and Biomedical Engineering, emeritus, at [[Washington University in St. Louis]], where he holds the [[Albert G. Hill|Albert Gordon Hill]] Endowed Chair in the Faculty of Arts and Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physics.wustl.edu/people/james-g-miller|title=James G. Miller|date=2018-06-20|website=Department of Physics|language=en|access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref> He is notable for his interdisciplinary contributions to [[biomedical physics]], [[echocardiography]], and [[Ultrasound|ultrasonics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://source.wustl.edu/2016/11/miller-receives-2016-rayleigh-award-international-ultrasonics-symposium/|title=Miller receives 2016 Rayleigh Award at International Ultrasonics Symposium {{!}} The Source {{!}} Washington University in St. Louis|date=2016-11-09|website=The Source|language=en-US|access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref>

== Biography ==

Miller grew up in [[St. Louis|St. Louis, Missouri]], and received his bachelor's degree in physics, summa cum laude, from [[Saint Louis University (United States)|Saint Louis University]] in 1964. He went on to receive master's and doctoral degrees from Washington University in St. Louis in 1966 and 1969, respectively.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://physics.wustl.edu/nd/fac/JimMiller2016RayleighAwardLetter.pdf|title=2016 Rayleigh Award - Wayback Machine|last=|first=|date=2018-06-07|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180607050415/http://physics.wustl.edu/nd/fac/JimMiller2016RayleighAwardLetter.pdf|archive-date=2018-06-07|access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref> His doctoral advisor was Daniel Isadore Bolef.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=85094|title=Physics Tree - James Gegan Miller|website=academictree.org|access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref>

Thereafter he was hired as assistant professor of physics and earned tenure 2 years later, in 1970.<ref name=":0" /> He is now Albert Gordon Hill Chair of the Faculty of Arts and Sciences and Director of the Laboratory of Ultrasonics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pages.wustl.edu/jamesgmiller|title=James G. Miller|website=pages.wustl.edu|access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref>

== Teaching ==
For about four decades, Miller taught a course titled "Physics of the Heart" at Washington University. He won the college's Faculty Teaching Award in 1989 and the Emerson Teaching Award in 2004. Over the course of his career, he mentored 35 graduate students and numerous undergraduates, including Nobel Laureate in Chemistry [[William E. Moerner]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2014/moerner/facts/|title=The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2014|website=NobelPrize.org|language=en-US|access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref>

== Research ==
Miller has published more than 165 refereed journal articles and 110 conference proceedings and book chapters.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pages.wustl.edu/jamesgmiller/publications|title=Publications List|last=Miller|first=James G.|date=|website=Washington University in St. Louis|access-date=|archive-date=2019-12-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191228043759/https://pages.wustl.edu/jamesgmiller/publications|url-status=dead}}</ref> His work has contributed greatly to ultrasonics, [[Cardiac muscle|myocardial tissue]] characterization and has been incorporated into [[echocardiography]] devices in use throughout the world.<ref name=":0" />
